chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Fazari narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Khalid al-Tameemi narrated to me, saying: Some of our companions narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from al-Ala' ibn Rizin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
For the Qa'im there are five signs: the appearance of al-Sufyani, and al-Yamani, the cry from the heaven, the killing of the pure soul, and the sinking in al-Bayda'.

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيُّ: Al-Sufyani, a prominent figure whose emergence is a major sign of the end times.
key_terms.الصَّيْحَةُ: The Cry, a celestial voice or sound announcing the truth or judgment.
key_terms.النَّفْسُ الزَّكِيَّةُ: The Pure Soul, a specific righteous individual who will be killed.
key_terms.الْبَيْدَاءُ: Al-Bayda', a specific desert area where a sinking (khasf) will occur.
key_terms.الْيَمَانِيُّ: Al-Yamani, a leader who will call people to the truth before the appearance of the Imam.

ai.seo_question: What are the five signs preceding the appearance of the Qa'im according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the five major signs preceding the reappearance of al-Qa'im, emphasizing the Sufyani and al-Yamani as pivotal political figures whose rise and fall frame the eschatological era. The inclusion of the 'Scream' (Sikha) and the 'Geological Sinking' (Khasf) highlights the cosmic and terrestrial upheavals that accompany the transition, while the martyrdom of the Pure Soul (Nafs al-Zakiyya) serves as a key spiritual catalyst. These events are central to Shia eschatology, illustrating the divine preparation of the world for the establishment of global justice.
